transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

That burning rubber smell almost always means the **drive belt** has snapped or stretched. The brush bar jams (usually with hair or string), the motor keeps turning, the belt slips and burns, then breaks. Suction through the hose still works because that's a separate fan motor.

**Check it (unplug first!)**
1. Flip the vacuum over and remove the base plate. On most Vax uprights it's a few screws or clips.
2. Look at the belt:
   - **Snapped, missing, shiny/glazed, cracked, or loose** → replace it.
   - **Looks fine** → check the brush bar instead (step 3).
3. Lift out the brush bar and spin it by hand. It should turn freely.
   - Cut off any wrapped hair or thread with scissors.
   - Clear fluff from the bearings/end caps at each end.
   - If it's stiff or grinding even when clean, the bearings are worn and the brush bar needs replacing.

**Replacing the belt**
- Find your model number on the sticker underneath or on the back.
- Search "Vax [model number] belt". They're cheap (a few quid/dollars), often sold in 2-packs.
- Loop the belt over the motor spindle, then stretch it onto the brush bar groove and click the bar back in. It'll be tight; that's normal.

**Before you buy anything, also check:**
- **Brush bar on/off switch or floor setting.** Some Vax models have a button or a "hard floor" mode that stops the brush.
- **Reset button.** Some newer Vax models (e.g. the Mach Air range) have a separate brush motor with an overload cut-out instead of a belt. If yours has no belt under the plate, clear any jam, leave it 30–60 min to cool, and look for a reset button near the brush head.

Tell me the model number and I can be more specific.
model is U85-AS-Be, its on the sticker on the back. il turn it over n have a look at the belt now

Nice, that's a **Vax Air Stretch** (U85-AS-Be is the Pet version), which uses a **belt-driven brush bar**, so a snapped or slipped belt fits your symptoms perfectly.

While you've got it flipped over:

- **Unplug it first.**
- The base plate is usually held by a few screws and/or clips. Undo them and lift the plate off.
- The belt runs from a small metal spindle (motor side) to a groove on the brush bar.

**What you'll likely find:**
- **Belt snapped or missing:** you'll need a new one. Bits of rubber may be lying around inside, so pull those out.
- **Belt off the brush bar but intact:** check if it's stretched or glazed (shiny, smooth, smells burnt). If so, replace it anyway. A stretched belt will just slip again.
- **Belt fine:** spin the brush bar by hand. Hair wrapped round it or jammed in the end caps is the usual cause.

**Getting the right belt:**
Search **"Vax Air Stretch U85-AS-Be belt"** and check the listing says it fits your model number. Pet models get hair wrapped round the brush bar a lot, so while it's apart, cut off any hair and clean out the ends of the bar. That'll stop the next belt burning out.

Let me know what you find under there.
ok looked under it. belt is snapped in 2 bits, one bit has a shiny melted looking edge. brushbar had loads of hair n a bit of tassel wrapped round the ends but ive cut it off and it spins free now

That confirms it: the tassel and hair jammed the brush bar, the belt slipped and melted against the spindle, then snapped. Since the brush bar now spins freely, a **new belt** should fix it.

**Before you fit the new belt**
- Remove all bits of the old belt, including any stuck inside the housing.
- Check the motor spindle (the small metal shaft the belt loops round). If there's melted rubber on it, carefully pick or scrape it off. Any left on there can make the new belt slip or wear quickly.
- Clean out any hair or fluff from the brush bar end caps and the slots they sit in.

**Ordering**
- Search **"Vax Air Stretch U85-AS-Be belt"** and make sure the listing names your model.
- Get a 2-pack if possible. They're cheap and it's handy to have a spare.
- Genuine Vax belts tend to last longer than the cheapest generic ones, but either will work.

**Fitting it**
1. Loop the belt round the motor spindle first.
2. Stretch it over the groove on the brush bar. It'll be tight, which is normal.
3. Seat the brush bar back into its slots so it clicks in at both ends.
4. Spin the brush bar by hand to check the belt runs straight and isn't twisted.
5. Refit the base plate.

**To stop it happening again**
- Avoid running over rug tassels, cables and loose threads.
- Cut hair off the brush bar every few weeks. With pets it builds up quickly.
- If it ever smells of burning rubber again, switch off straight away and check for a jam. Catching it early can save the belt.
